figures.finding: Nepal has no child-performer permit: no child under fourteen may be engaged in work as a labourer; a child of fourteen to sixteen may work only with the approval of the labour office and of a parent or guardian, never from 18:00 to 06:00, at most six hours a day and 36 a week, with half an hour's break after three hours and a day off each week. The Act binds 'enterprises' (any firm, company or organisation running an industry, business or service) and has no performing exception (reading: it reaches a film production company employing a child actor, writer or director alike).

from14to16.needs: labour office approval and parent or guardian approval

value.reachesWritingDirecting: yes, any work in an enterprise (reading)

figures.applies: Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act 2056 (2000) ss. 2, 3, 6, 9, FAOLEX English copy (later amendments not read).

sources.said: (a) "Child" means a minor not having completed the age of sixteen years. (b) "Enterprise" means any factory, organization, association, firm, company or their groups established as per prevailing law with objectives of operating any industry, business or service. ... 3. Child not to be Engaged in work:(1) No child having not attained the age of 14 years shall be engaged in works as a laborer. ... 6. Approval to be obtained : (1) In case any Enterprise has to engage a child in works, an approval has to be obtained from the concerned labor office or any authority or official prescribed by that office and form the father, mother or guardian of the child. ... Provided that no approval pursuant to this Section shall be required to engage a child in cultural programs or any activity for greater protection of interest of children to be organized by an academic institution approved by Government of Nepal or by an organization established according to the prevailing law for protection of rights or interests of children. ... 9. Time to Engage in works: (1) No child shall be engaged in work for a period after six o'clock at the evening to six o'clock at the morning. (2) No child shall be engaged in work for more than six hours in a day and more than thirty-six hours in a week
